figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. (A, B) Representative polyketide chain-fusion reactions:
Reactions catalyzed by (A) MxnB and (B) CsyB. (C) Structure of
gregatin A (1) and the previously suggested mechanism to generate
the furanone core of 1. (D) Alternative possible mechanism to
produce the backbone skeleton of 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. (A) Schematic representations of the grg cluster. HR-PKS:
highly reducing polyketide synthase; trans-ER: trans-acting enoylre-
ductase; TF: transcription factor; O-MT: O-methyltransferase; MFS:
major facilitator superfamily transporter; ABH: α/β hydrolase; P450:
cytochrome P450 monooxygenase. (B) HPLC proﬁles of culture
supernatant extracts from A. oryzae NSAR1 transformants. The
chromatograms were monitored at 230 nm. (C) Structures of the
metabolites isolated or detected in this study.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Isotope-labeling experiment of 1 using [1-13C] and [2-13C]
sodium acetate.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. In vitro reconstitution of the chain-fusion reaction. LC-MS
chromatograms of products from (A) reactions performed with
malonyl-CoA, NADPH, and SAM; (B) reactions of GrgF with the
substrate analogues 9 and 10; and (C) reactions of GrgF mutants.
The chromatograms were extracted at m/z 263.13. Compound 4
partially puriﬁed from the A. oryzae transformant was used as a
standard. (D) HPLC chromatograms of the products from the
reactions of GrgF and its mutants with 10. The chromatograms were
monitored at 280 nm. WT: wild-type enzyme. (E) Structures of
substrate analogues used in this study (9 and 10) and the predicted
structures of 11a and 11b.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. (A) Overall structure of GrgF. The core domain and lid
region are shown in pink and orange, respectively. One of the
monomers in the asymmetric unit is shown. (B) Probable substrate
binding site of GrgF. The lid region (orange) seals the hydrophobic
chamber (pink). The binding site was predicted using CASTp.17 (C)
Docked model of the C11 chain (cyan). C-1 is covalently bound to
Cys115.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. (A) Proposed biosynthetic pathway of the chain-fused product 4 and catalytic mechanism of GrgF. (B) Proposed late-stage biosynthesis
of gregatin A (1).
